inputs.text: Look at this absolute administrative mess. Over 58 lakh names were deleted during a revision exercise in West Bengal, exposing a system that is clearly failing the basic requirement of maintaining order and accountability. Now, instead of enforcing personal responsibility and fixing the rolls, we are bogged down by the courts and the state government haggling over where to set up tribunals that aren't even operational yet. The Supreme Court directed these tribunals, but their functioning details are still pending while they bicker over locations with the Calcutta High Court. Meanwhile, the software for voters to challenge rulings is ready, paving the way for endless procedural delays instead of restoring stability and trust for the citizens. This is what happens when progressive institutional machinery gets bogged down in bureaucracy while the foundational integrity of our civic duties is left hanging.
